english.title: Send letter / communication / article conveying a threatening message
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) sent to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..)

(A)_[a letter]_
(B)_[an electronic communication, namely **(..SPECIFY..),]_
(C)_[an article, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..),]_

which conveyed a threat for the purpose of causing distress or anxiety to the recipient or to any other person to whom you intended that it or its contents or nature should be communicated
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1)(a) and (4) of the Malicious Communications Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies after 30th January 2024 due to changes made by the Online Safety Act 2023. For the offence of sending a threatening communication under section 181 of the Online Safety Act 2023 applying after this date see H101562.
(ii) See section 1(2) of the Malicious Communications Act 1988 for defence.
(iii) The "article" may be of any description.
(iv) The electronic communication may include text messages, fax and e-mail.
(v) Consider section 127 of the Communications Act 2003 - offences regarding improper use of public electronic communications network and services. Although, note, offences under section 127(2)(a) and (b) of the Communications Act 2003 (H5557 and H5558) are also repealed by the Online Safety Act 2023.
(iv) For offences committed prior to 13th April 2015, offences under section 1 of the Malicious Communications Act 1988 were 'summary only' and subject to a six month time limit for prosecutions.
